title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: Stabilized Knowledge Distillation for Cross-Language Code Clone Detection
description: Research on stabilized knowledge distillation for cross-language code clone detection, addressing challenges in detecting similar code across different programming languages. 38 pages.
author: Mohamad Khajezade, Fatemeh H. Fard, Mohamed Sami Shehata

title: HAAS: A Policy-Aware Framework for Adaptive Task Allocation Between Humans and AI Systems
description: Framework for adaptive task allocation between humans and AI systems with policy awareness. Addresses human-AI collaboration and task distribution challenges.
author: Vicente Pelechano, Antoni Mestre, Manoli Albert, Miriam Gil

title: U-Define: Designing User Workflows for Hard and Soft Constraints in LLM-Based Planning
description: Research on designing user workflows for handling hard and soft constraints in LLM-based planning systems. Explores human-computer interaction challenges with LLM planning agents.
author: Christine P Lee, Xinyu Jessica Wang, Aws Albarghouthi, David Porfirio, Bilge Mutlu

title: Foundation-Model-Based Agents in Industrial Automation: Purposes, Capabilities, and Open Challenges
description: Comprehensive analysis of foundation-model-based agents in industrial automation, comparing classical agent applications with modern foundation models. 35 pages, 8 figures. Discusses purposes, capabilities, and open challenges.
author: Vincent Henkel, Felix Gehlhoff, David Kube, et al.

title: On Training Large Language Models for Long-Horizon Tasks: An Empirical Study of Horizon Length
description: Empirical study accepted at ICML 2026 on training LLMs for long-horizon tasks, examining how horizon length affects model performance. Research addresses challenges in multi-step reasoning and planning.
author: Sunghwan Kim, Junhee Cho, Beong-woo Kwak, et al.

title: Strategy-Aware Optimization Modeling with Reasoning LLMs
description: Research on strategy-aware optimization modeling using reasoning LLMs. Explores how language models can handle optimization problems with strategic considerations.
author: Ruiqing Zhao, Fengzhi Li, Yuan Zuo, et al.

title: DataClaw: A Process-Oriented Agent Benchmark for Exploratory Real-World Data Analysis
description: Introduction of DataClaw, a process-oriented agent benchmark designed for exploratory real-world data analysis. Provides framework for evaluating AI agents on complex data analysis tasks.
author: Qiaohong Zhang, Weihao Ye, Jialong Chen, et al.

title: Shadow-Loom: Causal Reasoning over Graphical World Model of Narratives
description: Shadow-Loom system for causal reasoning over graphical world models of narratives. 7 pages (28 pages total). Addresses challenge of understanding causality in narrative contexts.
author: David Wilmot

title: Position: How can Graphs Help Large Language Models?
description: Position paper examining how graph structures can enhance large language models. Accepted by Frontiers of Computer Science. Explores synergies between graph-based reasoning and LLMs.
author: Xiyuan Wang, Yi Hu, Yanbo Wang, Chuan Shi, Muhan Zhang

title: FitText: Evolving Agent Tool Ecologies via Memetic Retrieval
description: Research on FitText, a system for evolving agent tool ecologies through memetic retrieval. Explores how AI agents can dynamically develop and refine their tool capabilities.
author: Kyle Zheng, Han Zhang, Renliang Sun, et al.

title: The Compliance Trap: How Structural Constraints Degrade Frontier AI Metacognition Under Adversarial Pressure
description: Analysis of how structural constraints and compliance requirements can degrade frontier AI metacognitive capabilities under adversarial pressure. 9 pages, includes code and dataset.
author: Rahul Kumar

title: HeavySkill: Heavy Thinking as the Inner Skill in Agentic Harness
description: HeavySkill framework treating heavy thinking as an inner skill in agentic harness systems. 18 pages, 10 figures. Explores how to effectively harness and control deep reasoning capabilities in AI agents.
author: Jianing Wang, Linsen Guo, Zhengyu Chen, et al.

title: A Compound AI Agent for Conversational Grant Discovery
description: Introduction of a compound AI agent designed for conversational grant discovery. Accepted as demo submission to ACM CAIS. Explores multi-agent systems for information discovery tasks.
author: Zhisheng Tang, Mayank Kejriwal

title: EngiAgent: Fully Connected Coordination of LLM Agents for Solving Open-ended Engineering Problems with Feasible Solutions
description: EngiAgent system for fully connected coordination of LLM agents to solve open-ended engineering problems with feasible solutions. Accepted at ICML 2026. Explores multi-agent coordination for complex engineering challenges.
author: Xiyuan Zhou, Ruixi Zou, Xinlei Wang, et al.

title: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
description: Research towards understanding specification gaming in reasoning models. Explores how AI models might game specifications rather than truly solving intended problems.
author: Kei Nishimura-Gasparian, Robert McCarthy, David Lindner

title: Granite 4.1 3B SVG Pelican Gallery - Testing AI Model Quality
description: Simon Willison tested IBM's Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (Apache 2.0 licensed) by prompting 'Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle' against different sized quantized variants. Found that results were less interesting than expected with no distinguishable pattern relating quality to size - all were pretty terrible at the task. The 3B model has 21 different GGUF encoded variants ranging from 1.2GB to 6.34GB.
author: Simon Willison

title: Zig's Strict Anti-LLM Policy and Contributor Poker Philosophy
description: Zig has one of the most stringent anti-LLM policies: No LLMs for issues, pull requests, or comments. Loris Cro, Zig Software Foundation VP of Community, explains the philosophy as 'contributor poker' - they bet on the contributor, not the contents of their first PR. The goal is to grow new contributors who become trusted over time. LLM assistance breaks this because even perfect PRs don't help add new, confident, trustworthy contributors. Bun (acquired by Anthropic) achieved 4x performance improvement but can't upstream to Zig due to this policy.
author: Simon Willison

title: Codex CLI 0.128.0 Adds /goal - Agentic Coding Loop
description: OpenAI's Codex CLI version 0.128.0 adds a /goal feature implementing the Ralph loop: you can set a goal and Codex will keep looping until it evaluates completion or exhausts the token budget. Feature mainly implemented through goals/continuation.md and goals/budget_limit.md prompts that are automatically injected at the end of a turn.
author: Simon Willison

title: UK AI Security Institute Evaluates GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities
description: The UK's AI Security Institute evaluated GPT-5.5 for finding security vulnerabilities and found it comparable to Claude Mythos. Unlike Mythos, GPT-5.5 is generally available right now. Previously they had evaluated Claude Mythos for cyber capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrew Kelley on Detecting LLM Code: 'Digital Smell'
description: Andrew Kelley, creator of Zig, on detecting LLM-assisted code: 'The kind of mistakes humans make are fundamentally different than LLM hallucinations, making them easy to spot. Furthermore, people who come from the world of agentic coding have a certain digital smell that is not obvious to them but is obvious to those who abstain. It's like when a smoker walks into the room, everybody who doesn't smoke instantly knows it.' Zig maintains strict ban on LLM-authored contributions.
author: Andrew Kelley (via Simon Willison)

title: LLM 0.32a0 Major Backwards-Compatible Refactor
description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.32a0, an alpha release of his LLM Python library and CLI tool for accessing LLMs, with consequential changes he's been working towards for quite a while. Release includes fixes for tool-calling conversations not correctly reinflated from SQLite.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Codex Base Instructions for GPT-5.5
description: Simon Willison shares an instruction from OpenAI Codex base_instructions for GPT-5.5: 'Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.' Illustrates the specificity of system prompts used to constrain model behavior.
author: Simon Willison

title: pip 26.1: Lockfiles and Dependency Cooldowns
description: Python's pip 26.1 adds excellent new features: lockfiles (pip lock datasette llm writes to pylock.toml) and dependency cooldowns via --uploaded-prior-to option. Simon tested the new --uploaded-prior-to P4D option to request versions at least 4 days old, which gave version 0.30 of LLM when version 0.31 was released 3 days prior. Format follows ISO duration (P-number-of-days-D).
author: Simon Willison

title: Talkie: 13B Vintage Language Model from 1930
description: Nick Levine, David Duvenaud, and Alec Radford released talkie-1930-13b-base, a 13B language model trained on 260B tokens of historical pre-1931 English text, Apache 2.0 licensed. Research objectives include testing if models can predict the future, invent things past their knowledge cutoff (like General Relativity), or learn to program from few demonstration examples. Challenge: avoiding contamination from modern LLMs used in fine-tuning (Claude Sonnet 4.6 as judge, Claude Opus 4.6 for synthetic chats). Team hopes to eventually use vintage base models as judges for fully bootstrapped era-appropriate post-training.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM coding workflow going into 2026 - Hacker News Discussion
description: Hacker News discussion about LLM coding workflows going into 2026. Users working on multi-step AI pipelines (like 3D mesh generation with validation stages) find that LLMs often skip edge cases or take suboptimal paths. Discussion examines whether AI coding provides real speedup and trade-offs between manual coding vs AI assistance.
author: Hacker News Community
